problem: Learned waypoint predictors for image-goal navigation (GNM, ViNT, PlaceNav) output waypoints with no geometric guarantees: they can land on obstacles or deviate from the global path. Most pipelines also either lack a local planner or use fixed-parameter ones that cannot adapt to confined spaces.
motivation: Lightweight topological maps of geotagged images avoid precise metric maps and global localization, which makes them practical for indoor deployment. Learned waypoints still carry useful priors such as center-biased, smooth motion, so the paper corrects their geometric flaws instead of discarding them. Refinement outcomes are also informative for the local planner.
key_idea: Sample candidate waypoints along the skeleton of the segmented traversable region, score them together with the learned GNM waypoint on safety, direction coherence and prior fidelity, and use the refinement's clearance and correction magnitude to modulate the parameters of a Falco local planner.
insight: Direction coherence with the global path matters most: removing E_coher drops SR from 76.7 to 56.7 (10-20 m), because the agent overshoots turns and drifts beyond the map's coverage. Removing E_prior drops SR to 63.3, so the learned prior is worth keeping. Removing E_safe leaves SR unchanged but lowers SPL, because the downstream planner absorbs unsafe waypoints at a cost in efficiency. In the progressive ablation, a local planner alone (PlaceNav+Falco) reaches 56.7 SR, while refinement lifts it to 70.0, so the gains are not just from adding a planner.
method: Active subgoal retrieval: sequence-based VPR (MixVPR) localizes the robot on the topological map, Dijkstra gives the shortest path, and the node a fixed number of steps ahead becomes the subgoal image fed to GNM with the current image to predict a waypoint.

Localization filtering and relocalization: m_t = max(m_raw, m_{t-1}) blocks backward drift; if the index jumps more than j_max=4 nodes, the robot backtracks with buffered velocity commands, re-localizes on the full map with sequence VPR and replans.

Traversability-guided candidate sampling: DFormerV2 RGB-D segmentation gives a binary traversability map, whose morphological skeleton is sampled every 0.25 m; the GNM waypoint is added to the candidate set. A depth-consistency check (gamma=0.2) falls back to the raw GNM waypoint if segmentation looks unreliable.

Multi-criteria energy scoring: E = 0.5 E_safe + 1.5 E_coher + 1.0 E_prior. E_safe is a logistic penalty on clearance below d_safe=0.8 m, E_coher is the cosine misalignment with the global guidance vector, and E_prior is a logistic penalty on distance from the GNM waypoint beyond 2 d_safe. The argmin gives w*.
Falco trajectory-library planner: scores collision-free precomputed path groups by how well their endpoints reach w*, and retracts the search horizon if no path is free.

Adaptive planner modulation: clearance factor g_c and correction factor g_delta linearly interpolate trajectory scale S, collision tolerance N, planning horizon R and max velocity V between defaults and bounds, so small clearance gives compact, tolerant, slower planning.

setting.backbone: GNM (pretrained, frozen) + MixVPR + DFormerV2 segmentation + Falco planner
setting.training_data: Uses public pretrained weights with no fine-tuning; only the refinement hyperparameters were grid-searched on 5 held-out simulation scenes.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (90° FOV in sim, Orbbec Gemini335L on the real robot) plus a pre-collected topological map of geotagged images with poses
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (v, omega) from local trajectory selection toward refined waypoints
setting.privileged: Prior topological map with poses collected offline (image sequence at 0.25 m intervals); the shortest path for SPL is the Dijkstra path on this graph.

numbers.eval_set_note: 12 MP3D scenes, 30 episodes per method per difficulty level, short <10 m

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (12 MP3D scenes plus a real office), not a canonical benchmark; results are split by difficulty level. Split is labelled 'test' as no official split exists. Ablation and dynamic-obstacle results are omitted, though they appear in Tables IV-VII.
results: EgoNav beats every baseline at every distance in simulation and the real world. In simulation it reaches SR 96.7/76.7/60.0 versus 80.0/56.7/46.7 for the strongest baseline, PlaceNav+Falco. On the real humanoid it reaches SR 73.3/66.7/46.7 versus 60.0/50.0/33.3. The gains hold with dynamic obstacles (sim 10-20 m SR 63.3 vs 40.0).
limitations: Generalization is bounded by the waypoint predictor's training distribution, and the narrow field of view causes VPR failures when detours leave the map's visual coverage.
Open-loop backtracking only recovers from short detours of a few meters, and VPR degrades under lighting changes between map collection and navigation.
Dynamic-obstacle avoidance is only reactive (inherited from Falco), and the evaluation is small (30 episodes per cell), with no comparison to other adaptive planners.
